chapter: Early recordings and arrival in New York
title: Brunswick date with the Thornhill band: 'Don't Save Your Love for a Rainy Day'
summary: Listening to the Brunswick session; she thinks it a date Claude needed a singer for and may revive the song.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Yeah, that's favorite. Okay. Now you went into the recording studio again this time for the Brunswick Label, accompanied by the Claude Thornhill Band again, 26th of August 1937. And it's 'Don't Save Your Love for a Rainy Day,' which --
Okay, well how did that sound to you?
Oh boy. 'Don't Save Your Love for a Rainy Day' -- that's one I had completely forgotten about.
That must've been one of those dates that Claude had and he needed a singer, so he just reached out and grabbed me.
Well he couldn't have made a better choice. It was absolutely delightful.
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
I think I'll put that back into my repertoire. It's a good song.
